clue.text: Left scientific operation to sell back object of course

indicators.note: back says the joined pieces are read right to left

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory, is a scientific operation
flog is British slang for sell

explanation.surface: A researcher quits a lab venture and sells something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the whole string L + LAB + FLOG.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the ball is the thing being played, so an object belonging there.

clue.text: Material excavated around church provides pigment

indicators.note: around signals one piece placed about the other

parts.note: ore is mineral matter dug from the ground

explanation.surface: Diggings near a church yield a colouring agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown colouring made from iron-bearing clay.

clue.text: Defence establishment operated ancient computer software

parts.note: a fort is a military stronghold
ran, as in ran a machine, means operated

explanation.surface: A military base was running some very old programs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortran is a programming language from the 1950s, venerable by computing standards.

clue.text: Test cut — produced by swinging this tool?

indicators.note: swinging round suggests the letters turn back the other way
cut says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A trial chop made with the implement being swung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims EXAM to EXA, and 'swinging' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's surface describes a chopping implement swung by hand, which is what is meant.

clue.text: Artist identified by Cardinal on video broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter is recognised by a senior churchman appearing on a televised film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the fifteen letters of CARDINAL ON VIDEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance master who painted the Mona Lisa is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Get annoyed after study's coming out?

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first

parts.note: con is an old word for study; the 's simply joins it on
vex means annoy; the clue phrase stands for that verb

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated about a research paper being published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is not publication but bulging outward.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface that curves outward, like the back of a spoon, protrudes toward the viewer.

clue.text: Pleasant trees offloading top fruit

parts.note: clement means mild or pleasant, used of weather

indicators.note: offloading its top means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: pines are conifers

explanation.surface: Agreeable trees shed their uppermost produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offloading top' takes P from PINES, leaving INES.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small citrus fruits, a mandarin-orange hybrid.

clue.text: Accessory distinguishing close finish over dead-heat?

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: winning by a neck is a very close finish in horse racing
a tie is a contest ending level

explanation.surface: An item that separates two runners who crossed the line together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a band of cloth knotted at the collar, a common item of menswear.

clue.text: E, it seems, is a source of wonder

definitions.meaning: E is the letter that begins the word for the organ of sight
something surprising or revealing that makes one marvel

explanation.surface: A single letter is presented as something astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: E opens the word EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a revelation, something surprising and enlightening.

clue.text: Fill ward

definitions.meaning: to load a gun or top up a glass

explanation.surface: Two bare words, possibly a hospital instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To load is one sense, and a child under guardianship is the other.

clue.text: Nothing more elegant about college stage production

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: neater means tidier or more elegant

explanation.surface: Nothing is smarter than the play the college puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A short play in a single act is a kind of theatre production.

clue.text: Express disapproval of keeping one in decline

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within

parts.note: deprecate means express disapproval of
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Objecting to holding onto something while its value falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose value over time is to decline, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Cheat about to overlook one throttling favourite in race?

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round everything else

parts.note: con means cheat or swindle

indicators.note: throttling means gripping round the neck, so one piece holds another

parts.note: omit means overlook
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A swindler at the track ignores foul play against the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throttling' and 'about' are both containers: the favourite goes inside first, then the cheat wraps everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is one example of a contest, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Kind hearts not evident in tacky people

indicators.note: with their hearts gone, each word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Tasteless people show no generosity of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun kind means a sort or category, and this is a synonym.

clue.text: Is isle recalled in sea identified wrongly?

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the other

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A query whether an island in the sea has been mislabelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Given the wrong name is the same as wrongly identified.

clue.text: Periods of idleness in making arrangement for Toscanini

indicators.note: a musical arrangement hints that the conductor's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians rest while preparing an arrangement for the conductor Toscanini.
explanation.walkthrough: Arturo Toscanini was a famous Italian conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Instances of doing nothing are spells of idleness.

clue.text: Limit minister to restraining ambassador

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tend means minister to, look after
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told to hold back the envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is the last straw, quite beyond bearing, uses this idiom.

clue.text: Instinctive and simple to control time

indicators.note: to control means to hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated

explanation.surface: Someone is intuitive and artless about managing time.
explanation.definitionFit: An inborn ability, such as native wit, is instinctive.

clue.text: No good interrupting angry person without courtesy

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: irate means angry

explanation.surface: A worthless, cross person keeps cutting in rudely.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person lacks the courtesy of giving thanks.

clue.text: Make undrinkable tea, ruined in brewing? Not I

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so the letters are mixed
Not with I says that letter is left out of the mixed letters

explanation.surface: Someone spoils the tea while brewing, then denies responsibility.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TEA RUINED with the I left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial alcohol is treated with additives so it is unfit to drink.

clue.text: Kids besieging mother about beginning to choose pets?

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: tots are small children

indicators.note: about means wrapping round the following piece

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Children crowd round their mother as she starts picking animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Male cats are one kind of household animal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Family avoiding gambling male

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: staking money is gambling it
kin are family

explanation.surface: A man stays away from betting for his family's sake.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult male deer, or an unpartnered man at a party.

clue.text: Speculation, perhaps, one will get new clothing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a vestment is a garment, especially a priest's

explanation.surface: Guessing that someone will acquire fresh clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculation, putting money in for profit, is one example of this.

clue.text: Name only concocted to identify material

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A name invented purely to label some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic fabric used for stockings and much else.

clue.text: No place to overlook special symbols

indicators.note: to overlook means to miss out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: a station is a place or post

explanation.surface: There is no spot from which to look out over special signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of written signs, as in music or mathematics.

clue.text: Stud possibly staying in place

definitions.meaning: a stud farm is one example of a place where horses are kept

explanation.surface: A breeding horse is perhaps kept where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse establishment is one sense; steady and fixed is the other.

clue.text: Very positive concession

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
P abbreviates positive; the reversed letters at the start of this word are a coincidence

explanation.surface: A grant that is extremely favourable.
explanation.definitionFit: A small offering made to placate someone is a concession.

clue.text: Worried sailors about section aft

indicators.note: about means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: ate means worried, as in what's eating you
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Anxious sailors talk over a part of the ship at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at or toward the rear of a ship.

clue.text: Big mischief-maker failing to dislodge leader

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite

indicators.note: dislodging the leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: losing means failing

explanation.surface: A large troublemaker fails to unseat the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impressive in size or bearing is big.
